newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Selected buying helps Brussels bourse pare losses.
newsitem.headline: Selected buying helps Brussels bourse pare losses.

text.p: Selected buying, mostly by foreign brokers, helped the Brussels share market reverse losses in late trading on Thursday, but traders said the future course of the bourse remained open to question.
"There was an influx of purchases, mainly from overseas, that pushed up selected shares and helped the overall index end almost unchanged," one trader said.

"But I really think we are ahead of the fundamentals in Belgium so the market is at risk from any bad news. It is logical to take profits but people are still reluctant. I hope we consolidate now," he added.
The Bel-20 share index ended 1.32 points or just 0.06 percent down at 2,103.33 having moved in a 2,104.76/2,086.07 range. Approaching four billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.
The selective buying that lifted the index off the lows in the afternoon was targetted at financials, traders noted.

Kredietbank was a major beneficiary, ending nearly three percent up at 11,950 francs. But Groupe Bruxelles Lambert also added 15 francs to 4,765 and Generale Bank ended just 100 francs lower at 12,100 after at one stage losing 350 francs.
However, industrial stocks remained in the doldrums.

Metals group Union Miniere was 70 francs lower at 2,555 francs, cement group CBR was 75 francs off at 3,225, PetroFina was down 100 francs at 12,425 and chemical firm Solvay was 25 francs weaker at 21,500.
A clear exception was plastics firm Deceuninck which closed 1.8 percent up at 6,450 francs having at one stage hit a new high of 6,780 francs.
Traders gave various reasons for the strength of the share, ranging from players looking for plastics stocks to speculation the firm could be a takeover target.
